title: GitHub App Integration Audit v0
summary: Full integration audit and design map for the Rig Relay GitHub App across registration, permissions, webhooks, backend event handling, frontend UX, token/private-key storage, repository authorization, trace/evidence integration, and release gates. This is an audit/design document, not an implementation.

app_registration.notes: Private app initially, public later. Owned by personal developer account initially; migrate to Rig Relay organization later if desired. Homepage URL is the live Rig Relay static docs site. Webhook URL needed for hosted/relay endpoint; local dev requires tunnel or webhook replay strategy. User authorization deferred unless acting on behalf of individual users is needed. Device flow deferred unless CLI/login needs it. Installation visibility starts private/internal.

permission_profiles.title: Observe Public Repository
permission_profiles.description: Read repository metadata and events for public repos. No write access.
permission_profiles.use_case: Initial connection: let Rig observe repository events without asking for broad PATs. Maps pushes, PRs, checks, comments into Rig evidence.
permission_profiles.rationale: Minimum permissions required for event observation. Contents read is needed for reading repository files through the API. Checks read is needed for observing CI/check outputs. Issues read is needed for issue comment observation if used for agent collaboration.
risks: Contents read exposes repository source code to the Rig process
Event payloads may contain sensitive commit metadata
Scope creep if additional read permissions are requested later without profile audit
permission_profiles.user_consent_copy: Rig Relay will observe repository events (pushes, pull requests, checks) to build local evidence. No code or repository content will be sent to external services. All processing is local.

permission_profiles.title: Evidence Status Reporter
permission_profiles.description: Post Rig status/check outputs back to GitHub after local validation. Adds write access for checks/statuses.
permission_profiles.use_case: Rig completes local validation, creates check run or commit status on GitHub with results.
permission_profiles.rationale: Checks write allows creating annotated check runs. Commit statuses write allows posting status to PRs. Both are required for the evidence feedback loop: Rig validates locally, reports results to GitHub.
risks: Write access to checks/statuses could be misused to post misleading status
Check run annotations could expose local file paths or internal state
Need approval gate before any automated status posting
permission_profiles.user_consent_copy: Rig Relay will post check runs and commit statuses to GitHub with validation results. No code or internal file paths will be included in status reports.

permission_profiles.title: Governed Pull Request Assistant
permission_profiles.description: Create branches, PRs, and comments only after explicit user approval. Highest-risk profile with write access.
permission_profiles.use_case: Rig proposes a code change, user approves via desktop cockpit, Rig creates branch, commits changes, opens PR, and comments with evidence.
permission_profiles.rationale: Contents write is required for branch/commit creation. Pull requests write for PR creation. Issues write for commenting on PRs/issues. All write actions are gated behind explicit user approval in the cockpit.
risks: Contents write is the highest-risk permission — allows pushing commits
Pull requests write could be misused to modify or close PRs
Requires robust approval UI and audit trail
Requires worktree isolation to prevent dirty-file corruption
permission_profiles.user_consent_copy: Rig Relay may create branches, commits, and pull requests on your behalf. Every write action requires explicit approval in the desktop cockpit. You can review the full diff before approving. All actions are recorded in the local evidence store.

permission_profiles.title: Admin Avoidance Profile
permission_profiles.description: Explicitly documents permissions Rig should NOT request for v0. Serves as a safety checklist.
permission_profiles.use_case: Prevent accidental permission escalation. Audited against every implementation phase.
permission_profiles.rationale: Administration, Secrets, Actions write, Workflows write, Deployments write, Repository rules write, and Organization members write must never be requested in v0. These permissions grant broad mutation authority that violates Rig's governed, approval-gated design. Pages/webhooks write could interfere with GitHub Pages publishing or webhook configuration. Security events read could expose vulnerability data.
risks: Accidental inclusion in permission manifest during implementation
Organization-level permissions could be requested by mistake if owner_type is organization
Future phases may need to revisit specific avoidance items with new threat model
permission_profiles.user_consent_copy: Rig Relay does not request administration, secrets, actions, workflows, deployments, repository rules, or organization member permissions.

security_controls.title: Webhook Signature Verification
security_controls.description: Verify X-Hub-Signature-256 header using webhook secret and HMAC-SHA256. Use timing-safe comparison (hmac.compare_digest). Reject before JSON parsing.

security_controls.title: Reject Missing/Invalid Signature Before Processing
security_controls.description: If X-Hub-Signature-256 is missing or signature does not match, return 401 immediately. Never parse payload body before signature verification.

security_controls.title: Delivery Deduplication
security_controls.description: Deduplicate webhook deliveries by X-GitHub-Delivery header. If delivery ID already exists in event ledger, ignore (idempotent).

security_controls.title: Installation/Repository Authorization Check
security_controls.description: Before processing any webhook event, verify installation id is known and repository (if present) is in authorized list.

security_controls.title: Minimum Necessary Permissions
security_controls.description: Every permission requested in the GitHub App manifest must be justified by a specific use case. Never request permissions from admin_avoidance_profile. Audit permissions against current profile at installation time.

security_controls.title: Installation Token Memory Cache Only
security_controls.description: Installation access tokens stored only in memory cache with expiry. Never written to disk, keyring, or environment variables. Memory cache cleared on process exit.

security_controls.title: Private Key Outside Repo
security_controls.description: Private key stored in OS keyring (keychain://) or in file path outside repository. Key reference only in config. Never committed to git. File permissions must be 600 or stricter.

security_controls.title: No Secrets in Frontend Projection
security_controls.description: Frontend projections must never contain private key material, webhook secrets, installation tokens, or raw webhook payloads. Content-light projections only.

security_controls.title: No Raw Payload in Frontend by Default
security_controls.description: Raw webhook payloads are never projected to the frontend. Only event metadata (type, repository, timestamp, status) is shown.

security_controls.title: Write Actions Require Explicit User Approval
security_controls.description: Any action that creates branches, commits, PRs, comments, or modifies GitHub state must receive explicit user approval through the cockpit. No automated write actions.

security_controls.title: GitHub Payloads Treated as Untrusted Context
security_controls.description: Content from GitHub webhook payloads and API responses is treated as untrusted when fed into agent context. Sanitize, validate, and trace sources.

security_controls.title: Rate Limit and Backoff Handling
security_controls.description: Respect GitHub API rate limits. Implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429 responses. Monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining header.

security_controls.title: Payload Size Cap Under 25 MB
security_controls.description: Enforce a local payload size cap (e.g., 5 MB) well under GitHub's 25 MB limit. Reject oversized payloads before processing.

security_controls.title: Content-Light Trace Events with Correlation
security_controls.description: All GitHub App trace events are content-light. Include correlation fields (trace_id, github_delivery_id, github_installation_id, github_repository_id). Never include secrets, tokens, or raw payloads.

risks.title: Private Key Compromise
risks.description: If the GitHub App private key is compromised, an attacker can generate JWTs, obtain installation tokens, and read/write to all installed repositories. This is the highest-value secret in the GitHub App integration.
mitigations: Private key in OS keyring, never in repo
Never in trace events, logs, or frontend
Detection test for PEM in repo

risks.title: Webhook Secret Compromise
risks.description: If the webhook secret is compromised, an attacker can forge webhook events and inject malicious data into the Rig event store.
mitigations: Webhook secret in keyring or env, never in repo
Never in trace events or frontend

risks.title: Installation Token Leakage
risks.description: If an installation access token leaks to disk, logs, or frontend, an attacker with local access can use it to access repositories until it expires (1 hour).
mitigations: Never in trace events or frontend
Short expiry (1 hour, cache with 55-min TTL)

risks.title: Unauthorized Write Actions
risks.description: An agent or bug could create branches, commits, or PRs without explicit user approval, violating the governed write model.
mitigations: Explicit user approval required for every write action
Audit trail for every write proposal

risks.title: Context Poisoning via GitHub Events
risks.description: Malicious or crafted GitHub event payloads (PR descriptions, commit messages, issue comments) could inject harmful context into the agent's prompt.
mitigations: GitHub payloads treated as untrusted context

risks.title: Webhook Payload DoS
risks.description: Large webhook payloads (near 25 MB GitHub cap) could consume excessive memory or disk, or block the webhook processing pipeline.
mitigations: Content-light event ledger (no raw payload storage)

risks.title: GitHub API Rate Limit Exhaustion
risks.description: Excessive API calls for token exchange or status posting could exhaust rate limits, degrading the integration.
mitigations: Token cache with expiry (reuse within window)

risks.title: Permission Scope Creep
risks.description: Over time, new features may request additional permissions without proper audit, gradually expanding the attack surface.
mitigations: Admin avoidance profile as canonical deny-list
Permission audit on every profile change
Permission diff detection on installation update

open_questions.question: Should the webhook endpoint be a local HTTP server, or should Rig use smee.io / a tunnel for local development?
open_questions.context: GitHub requires a publicly reachable URL for webhook delivery. Local development without a public URL needs a tunnel or webhook replay strategy.

open_questions.question: How should the private key be provisioned — user downloads from GitHub and provides path, or Rig guides through GitHub App creation flow?
open_questions.context: The private key is generated by GitHub at app creation time and downloaded once. Rig needs to receive this key without the user copy-pasting raw PEM into a text field.

open_questions.question: Should Rig support multiple GitHub App installations across different accounts/orgs simultaneously?
open_questions.context: A user might want to observe repos from personal account and organization. Supporting multiple installations increases complexity.

open_questions.question: Should the write-approval model support time-bound or scope-bound pre-approval (e.g., 'approve all check-run postings for the next hour')?
open_questions.context: Frequent approval prompts could degrade UX. Pre-approval with constraints could balance safety and usability.

open_questions.question: Is the GitHub App integration required to be available in local-only mode (no internet), or can it require connectivity?
open_questions.context: Rig Relay defaults to local-only. GitHub App integration inherently requires network access. Should Rig gracefully degrade when offline?
